options.title: How Did a Train With No One Aboard Reach Lac-Mégantic?
options.first_line: A train with no one aboard hit sixty-five miles an hour as it entered Lac-Mégantic. How?
options.first_frame: Night, 3D: a black crude-oil train races past the camera toward the lights of Lac-Mégantic, the locomotive's cab lit and empty, a speed dial climbing beside it, the caption 'JULY 2013 · LAC-MÉGANTIC, QUEBEC' and the reconstruction tag.

options.title: The Lac-Mégantic Train That Rolled Away on Its Own
options.first_line: Lac-Mégantic, Quebec. A parked oil train starts to roll, and nobody is on it. Why?
options.first_frame: Night, 3D close-up: the brake shoe on a tank-car wheel lifts away and the wheel begins to turn, the train's name and place typing on in mono, the reconstruction tag top left.

options.title: Why Was Nobody Driving the Lac-Mégantic Train?
options.first_line: The train that reached Lac-Mégantic had no driver. He had left it on a hill for the night. So what let it go?
options.first_frame: Night, 3D wide: the empty locomotive at the head of a long line of tank cars on a dark hillside, its cab light on, a single amber hand-brake wheel glowing on the last car, the place and date caption.

why: An empty, lit cab racing at night toward a named town makes a stranger ask how a train with no one aboard got there, and neither the title nor the first frame gives away the answer, while B's lifting brake shoe and C's left-on-a-hill line and glowing hand-brake wheel hint at the cause.
